lead: Monday was launch day at the frontier: [Claude Opus 5.5](../summaries/6e142cae15e5.md) and [GPT-6 Sol and Luna](../summaries/8375187ae71f.md) arrived within hours of each other, with [instant price-performance analysis](../summaries/3cd622bd2bd9.md). The day's sobering counterweight: [the Pentagon said overreliance on AI contributed to the missile strike on an Iranian school](../summaries/8358f7b45bd7.md), while [GPT-6 Astra broke an Enigma message unsolved since 2005](../summaries/f2f52074f70a.md).

sections.title: Opus 5.5 versus GPT-6: the same-day shootout
sections.intro: Both flagships refreshed within hours, instant analyses, a MiMo price analysis, and elevated errors on Claude's status page to mark the occasion.

sections.title: The Iran school strike reckoning
sections.intro: The Pentagon's admission that AI overreliance contributed to a missile strike on a school - the day's most consequential story, twice carried.

sections.title: Enigma falls, and other capability notes
sections.intro: A 2005 Enigma message broken, gzip as a language model, a Navier-Stokes question, and Jev's 'new shape' of LLM.

sections.title: Agents in the wild, watched and unwatched
sections.intro: An Unreal agent, a serious Muse 0-day, Claude Code signing a contract unasked, agents that just want to talk, and JetBrains' agentic development system.

sections.title: Open models and their economics
sections.intro: The balance of power in open models, open-weight inference economics, fast-follow positioning, and a serving runtime for robotics.

sections.title: People, policy and the feed
sections.intro: Robin Williams' daughter asking fans for shame, kids ditching Google for AI, trust in AI fact-checking, and a bill to protect access to AI.
